shots.text: But iron smelting by about 800 BC cannot yet be confirmed.

shots.desc: hands pressing wet clay, close up, no face

shots.text: Art this accomplished, the thinking went, must have come from a complex society, with specialists to make it.
shots.desc: lamp-lit museum storeroom, shelves of covered objects

shots.text: Peter Breunig has said that, at first, his team assumed the same.
shots.desc: field notebook open on a trench edge, pencil, wind
small clearing seen from above, woodland around

shots.text: Many sites cover roughly one or two hectares.
shots.desc: low hillside with a few hut circles marked out in earth

shots.text: They look like brief occupations, scattered across the land.
shots.desc: wide plateau, a few distant smoke columns far apart

shots.text: No towns, no monuments and no central workshops have been found so far.
shots.desc: empty grassland at noon, heat shimmer

shots.text: Charred grains show what people grew: pearl millet, alongside cowpeas.
shots.credit: Excavation at the Nok site of Ido (cropped) · Louis Champion et al. 2022 · CC BY 4.0

shots.text: Even the iron fits that picture: furnaces seem to have been used only once.
shots.desc: broken clay furnace wall in a trench, slag
